title: Long AVGO — ISM 54.0 Confirms AI Hardware Cycle; Custom ASIC + Networking Reentry at Range Support
entry: Long $368–385 (AVGO at ~$375 on July 1, consolidating flat after the June correction from $410+). Entry is the retest of the June 2026 base after the prior AVGO long positions (June 1, June 4) were closed on stops during the FOMC-driven correction. ISM 54.0 is the re-entry signal: manufacturing expansion at a 37-month high directly validates the hyperscaler AI infrastructure investment cycle that drives AVGO's custom ASIC and networking revenue. Scale: 70% initial on July 1–2; 30% add if AVGO dips to $368–372 post-NFP. Do NOT initiate above $390 — above that level the post-ISM premium has exceeded the first trade zone and the entry is chasing ISM euphoria rather than rebuying the base.
stop_loss: $348 daily close (~7.2% below $375) — implies (1) NFP July 2 prints a recession signal (<80K) that forces hyperscalers to defer AI capex guidance, directly threatening AVGO's custom ASIC design win revenue timeline; (2) a hyperscaler (Meta, Google, Microsoft, Amazon) announces a pause or reduction in AI infrastructure capex at an upcoming conference or investor day, removing the demand signal that the ISM 54.0 expansion thesis validates; or (3) Broadcom Q3 2026 earnings (scheduled September) pre-announce revenue below the $15.9B consensus, indicating AI networking orders have plateaued ahead of the next-gen transition.
targets: $402 — ISM expansion narrative sustains through Q3: hyperscaler AI capex guidance raised at July earnings calls (META July 29, MSFT July 30, GOOGL July 29, AMZN July 30); AVGO AI networking and custom ASIC orders re-accelerate with each hyperscaler beat; +7.2% from $375; take 40% of position

$432 — Q3 2026 earnings beat (September): Broadcom AI revenue (custom ASIC + networking) exceeds $8B for the first time in a single quarter; VMware integration complete and software revenue growing double-digits; sell-side raises price targets across the board; +15.2%; take 40%

$462 — Custom ASIC TAM expansion: 3 hyperscalers simultaneously announce next-generation ASIC programs (beyond the current Google TPU v5 / Meta MTIA generation) with AVGO as the manufacturing partner; AVGO custom ASIC TAM revised from $30B to $50B+ by 2028; multiple re-rates to 28x forward; +23.2%; exit final 20%
catalyst: ISM Manufacturing June 2026: 54.0 (37-month high, beat vs 53.0 consensus, sixth consecutive expansion month). This is the primary re-entry trigger. Manufacturing expansion at this level directly validates the AI capex investment cycle: hyperscalers (Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon) confirm AI infrastructure investment when they see their enterprise customers expanding production — the 54.0 ISM print is the demand confirmation that CEO confidence in AI ROI is justified. Broadcom is the direct beneficiary as the supplier of custom AI chips (ASIC) and AI networking silicon (Tomahawk, Jericho) to every major hyperscaler. The secondary catalyst window is Q3 2026 earnings (September), where Broadcom AI revenue is expected to cross the $8B quarterly threshold for the first time.
thesis:
Broadcom is the cleanest expression of the AI hardware cycle at a company that is NOT NVDA — meaning it has not run 300% in the prior 18 months, does not carry Blackwell execution risk, and has not already priced in the entire 2026–2028 AI capex cycle. AVGO at $375 is approximately 23x forward earnings, well below NVDA's 35x+ and AMD's 40x+, yet AVGO's AI revenue is growing at a similar rate through a different and more durable mechanism: custom ASIC design wins and networking silicon are embedded in hyperscaler infrastructure for 5-year cycles, not subject to the quarterly allocation competition that makes NVDA's H100/H200/Blackwell demand more volatile.

The ISM 54.0 print is the macro catalyst for re-entry. The six consecutive months of manufacturing expansion means the US industrial economy is not contracting — and AI infrastructure is the most active form of US manufacturing investment in 2026. Google's TPU v5, Meta's MTIA, and Amazon's Trainium are all Broadcom-dependent at the networking layer even when the ASIC is custom. Broadcom's Tomahawk 5 (800G networking) is the standard switching fabric for AI clusters regardless of whether the GPU is NVDA, AMD, or custom — making AVGO's networking franchise more durable than any single GPU supplier's position.

The re-entry is at range support, not at a breakout. AVGO was stopped out of the prior long (June 4 position) at approximately $340–350 during the FOMC-driven correction. The stock has since recovered to $375 — back within the original thesis range but below the prior $400+ highs. This is not a chase; it is a return to the base after the macro correction resolved in AVGO's favor. The ISM 54.0 print directly validates the hyperscaler AI capex thesis that the June FOMC correction temporarily disrupted.

The July 29–30 hyperscaler earnings window (META, GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN all reporting within 48 hours) is the next formal catalyst: if three or four of the five hyperscalers raise AI capex guidance simultaneously, AVGO's 2026–2027 AI revenue estimates are raised across the sell-side in a compressed period, driving a rapid re-rating. The custom ASIC portion of AVGO's AI revenue (currently ~40% of total AI revenue) is the highest-margin, stickiest component — and each design win has a 3–5 year sole-source relationship. The TAM for custom AI ASICs is currently estimated at $30B by 2027; the actual realized number could be significantly higher if the ISM expansion signals persistent manufacturing AI adoption.
bull_case: Hyperscaler earnings July 29–30 all raise 2026 AI capex guidance: META to $125B+, MSFT and GOOGL each above $75B for the year. AVGO sell-side estimates for FY2026 AI revenue raised from $30B toward $35B. Q3 earnings (September) confirm AI networking at $8B quarterly run-rate. AVGO re-rates toward 26x forward, reaching $432 (Target 2). Custom ASIC TAM expansion announcement at Hot Chips (August) drives AVGO to $462 (Target 3) as the blue-sky scenario of $50B+ 2028 custom ASIC TAM becomes consensus.
bear_case: NFP July 2 prints recession signal (<80K). Hyperscalers signal AI capex pauses on the July 29–30 calls — not hikes. The AI infrastructure cycle that ISM 54.0 confirmed for manufacturing does not translate to software/cloud capex maintenance. AVGO's custom ASIC design win pipeline slows as hyperscalers defer next-gen programs from H2 2026 to 2027. AVGO falls back to $348–350 (stop zone) as the networking and ASIC thesis is deferred rather than validated.
invalidation: $348 daily close; OR any two of the four hyperscalers (META, GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN) reduce or freeze AI capex guidance on the July 29–30 earnings calls (direct demand destruction for AVGO AI revenue); OR Broadcom announces a supply chain issue with the Tomahawk 5 ramp (manufacturing yield at TSMC constraining networking silicon output); OR ISM July 2026 prints below 50.0 (contradicts the expansion thesis that drove today's re-entry).
